```plato

    // Hooke's law for an isotropic material: twice the shear modulus times the
    // strain, plus the first Lame parameter times the volumetric strain on the
    // diagonal.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hooke%27s_law#Isotropic_materials)
    ToStressState(strain: StrainState3D, moduli: LameParameters): StressState3D
    {
        var e = strain.Matrix;
        var twoMu = 2.0 * moduli.ShearModulus.Pascals;
        var volumetric = moduli.FirstParameter.Pascals * (e.M11 + e.M22 + e.M33);
        return StressState3D(SymmetricMatrix3x3(
            twoMu * e.M11 + volumetric, twoMu * e.M12, twoMu * e.M13,
            twoMu * e.M22 + volumetric, twoMu * e.M23,
            twoMu * e.M33 + volumetric));
    }

    // The von Mises equivalent stress: the single number whose value at yield
    // equals the uniaxial yield strength, and the reading a result plot is
    // normally coloured by. It ignores hydrostatic pressure, so a body squeezed
    // equally from every side reads zero however hard it is squeezed.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Von_Mises_yield_criterion)
    VonMisesStress(stress: StressState3D): Pressure
    {
        var s = stress.Matrix;
        var normal = (s.M11 - s.M22).Square + (s.M22 - s.M33).Square + (s.M33 - s.M11).Square;
        var shear = s.M12.Square + s.M23.Square + s.M13.Square;
        return Pressure((0.5 * normal + 3.0 * shear).Sqrt);
    }

    // The constant in-plane strain inside one plane triangle. ShearXY is the
    // ENGINEERING shear strain (twice the tensor component), which is what
    // `StrainState2D` documents.
    ElementStrain(f: TriangleFace, positions: Array<Point2D>,
        displacements: Array<Vector2D>): StrainState2D
    {
        var gradients = f.ShapeGradients(positions);
        var nodes = f.Vertices;
        var nodal = 3.MapRange(i => Vector3D(displacements[nodes[i].Value].X,
            displacements[nodes[i].Value].Y, 0.0));
        return StrainState2D(
            DisplacementGradient(nodal, gradients, 0, 0),
            DisplacementGradient(nodal, gradients, 1, 1),
            DisplacementGradient(nodal, gradients, 0, 1)
                + DisplacementGradient(nodal, gradients, 1, 0));
    }

    // Hooke's law in the plane, using the Lame pair of the model's idealization.
    ToStressState(strain: StrainState2D, moduli: LameParameters): StressState2D
    {
        var lambda = moduli.FirstParameter.Pascals;
        var twoMu = 2.0 * moduli.ShearModulus.Pascals;
        return StressState2D(
            Pressure((lambda + twoMu) * strain.NormalX + lambda * strain.NormalY),
            Pressure(lambda * strain.NormalX + (lambda + twoMu) * strain.NormalY),
            Pressure(twoMu * strain.ShearXY * 0.5));
    }

    // The out-of-plane normal stress that accompanies a plane state: zero under
    // plane stress by definition, and Poisson's ratio times the sum of the
    // in-plane normal stresses under plane strain, where it is the out-of-plane
    // STRAIN that is zero instead. This is the one reading a plane state cannot
    // supply on its own, and it is why von Mises stress in the plane needs the
    // idealization and the material as well as the stress.
    OutOfPlaneStress(stress: StressState2D, condition: PlaneCondition,
        poissonRatio: Number): Pressure
        => match (condition)
        {
            PlaneStress => Pressure(0.0);
            PlaneStrain => Pressure(poissonRatio
                * (stress.NormalX.Pascals + stress.NormalY.Pascals));
        };

    // The plane state widened to a full stress tensor by the out-of-plane normal
    // stress its idealization implies. Explicit, and taking that stress as a
    // parameter, because a plane state does not carry it.
    // Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - Conversions.
    ToStressState3D(stress: StressState2D, normalZ: Pressure): StressState3D
        => StressState3D(SymmetricMatrix3x3(
            stress.NormalX.Pascals, stress.ShearXY.Pascals, 0.0,
            stress.NormalY.Pascals, 0.0,
            normalZ.Pascals));

    // The full stress tensor inside one face of a solved plane model.
    ElementStress(f: TriangleFace, model: ElasticModel2D,
        displacements: Array<Vector2D>): StressState3D
    {
        var plane = f.ElementStrain(model.Mesh.Positions, displacements)
            .ToStressState(model.Moduli);
        return plane.ToStressState3D(
            plane.OutOfPlaneStress(model.Condition, model.Material.PoissonRatio));
    }

    //==
    // # Reading a solution
    //
    // The per-element and per-node arrays a result view consumes, and the
    // deformed geometry it draws.

    // The von Mises stress in every cell of a solved solid model, in cell order.
    VonMisesStresses(model: ElasticModel3D, solution: ElasticSolution3D): Array<Pressure>
    {
        var moduli = model.Material.ToLameParameters;
        return model.Mesh.Cells.Map(c =>
            c.ElementStrain(model.Mesh.Positions, solution.Displacements)
                .ToStressState(moduli).VonMisesStress);
    }

    // The von Mises stress in every face of a solved plane model, in face order.
    VonMisesStresses(model: ElasticModel2D, solution: ElasticSolution2D): Array<Pressure>
        => model.Mesh.Faces.Map(f =>
            f.ElementStress(model, solution.Displacements).VonMisesStress);

    // The magnitude of the displacement at each node of a solid model.
    DisplacementMagnitudes(solution: ElasticSolution3D): Array<Length>
        => solution.Displacements.Map(v => Length(v.Magnitude));

    // The magnitude of the displacement at each node of a plane model.
    DisplacementMagnitudes(solution: ElasticSolution2D): Array<Length>
        => solution.Displacements.Map(v => Length(v.Magnitude));

    // The mesh with every position moved by its displacement, exaggerated by
    // `scale`. A scale of 1 is the true deformed shape, which for a working
    // structure is far too small to see; anything larger is a picture, not a
    // geometry, and should say so.
    DeformedMesh(mesh: TetrahedralMesh3D, solution: ElasticSolution3D,
        scale: Number): TetrahedralMesh3D
        => TetrahedralMesh3D(
            mesh.Positions.Zip(solution.Displacements, (p, d) => p + d * scale),
            mesh.Cells);

    // The plane mesh with every position moved by its displacement, exaggerated
    // by `scale`.
    DeformedMesh(mesh: TriangleMesh2D, solution: ElasticSolution2D,
        scale: Number): TriangleMesh2D
        => TriangleMesh2D(
            mesh.Positions.Zip(solution.Displacements, (p, d) => p + d * scale),
            mesh.Faces);
```
